synthesis: The source links its smoothing levels in a concrete chain. Mellin contour displacement expresses the exponentially smoothed von Mangoldt discrepancy through separately classified residues, and Bernoulli subtraction removes the regular and trivial-zero contribution. Under RH, zero-counting and tail control then let a low conjugate pair force two-sided oscillation at the smoothing scale. Riesz averaging produces an absolutely convergent zero series and, later, the cumulative bound needed to make the correction term lower order when passing from the logarithmically weighted count through the prime-power count to pi(x)-Li(x). Smoothing therefore determines both where zero phases can be controlled and whether sign-sensitive information survives return to a sharper counting representation.

synthesis: The source exhibits two distinct, non-interchangeable routes from zero information to arithmetic sign phenomena. For the Dirichlet-L prime race, a completed product bounds the aggregate zero contribution, a prime-power split isolates the prime layer, and positive integral kernels preserve the resulting one-sided lower bound while inserting power and logarithmic convergence factors. For the zeta prime-counting error, truncation makes simultaneous phase recurrence finite-dimensional, a separate tail estimate restores the full sine series, and a modified Lindelof argument transports interior growth to a boundary limit that is not uniformly continuous. Read together, the sections show why a zero expansion alone does not give an arithmetic sign conclusion: one route preserves a bias through coefficient reweighting, while the other creates and transfers two-sided oscillation through phase recurrence and boundary control.
source_support: Units u07-u08 derive the conditional signed prime-power formula from L'/L, use the completed L-function product to bound zero residues, split the m=1, m=2, and m>=3 layers, and apply two positive integral representations to reach the smoothed unweighted prime-race series. Units u18-u19 instead express the normalized psi error as a zero-ordinate sine series, align a finite block by Dirichlet simultaneous approximation after controlling its tail, and use exponential damping plus two nested rectangles to pass the resulting interior Omega growth to the discontinuous boundary series.
nonparaphrase_operation: Completed-product control, exponent decomposition, and positive convergence kernels preserve a one-sided residue-class bias; independently, finite phase alignment, tail control, damping, and a modified boundary maximum principle produce and transport two-sided zeta-driven oscillation.
limits: These are parallel mechanisms, not one proof chain. The u07-u08 result assumes the Dirichlet-L analogue of RH and gives an eventual smoothed residue-class bias, not prime-race reversals; the predicted converse when that hypothesis fails is explicitly unproved. The u18-u19 route is the RH-simplified psi(x)-x oscillation argument along sequences, not a Dirichlet-L prime race. Thus the candidate title is broader than the supported relation. Exact kernel formulas, constants, and some growth scales are OCR-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted as a concrete contrast and refinement across the four parents, not as a claim that their theorems are identical. Each paired route needs multiple distinct units, and their joint evidence isolates two different missing bridges between zero terms and arithmetic signs. The synthesis expressly rejects the unsupported implication that boundary recurrence proves literal prime-race reversals.

synthesis: Section 3 builds a reusable localization calculus for oscillatory contour integrals, and Section 4 repurposes that calculus to obtain short-interval critical-line zero information. The first stage reduces power-weighted zero sums to cumulative control, converts the hard unweighted case to a von Mangoldt Dirichlet series, discards controlled contour pieces, and isolates the only coherent stationary range with a finite error ledger. The later stage defines a real critical-line transform, bounds its signed integral by splitting the associated Dirichlet-series phases around at most one stationary frequency, and observes that constant sign would remove cancellation. A second contour evaluation then supplies a main term proportional to the interval length, contradicting the small signed-integral bound and forcing an odd-order zero.
source_support: Unit u14 uses partial summation to reduce the weighted family to the omega=0 cumulative estimate while preserving uniformity in the phase parameter. Unit u15 proves that hard estimate by a zeta'/zeta rectangle, bounds the left, horizontal, and local-zero pieces, expands the right edge into von Mangoldt frequencies, and treats the stationary center and nonstationary tails through five error sums. Unit u16 turns a short signed integral of the real function X(t) into a sign-change criterion and evaluates the constant-sign comparison integral by a second rectangle as 2H+O(1). Unit u17 supplies the needed signed-integral estimate by Stirling reduction and a three-way frequency split with at most one stationary term, yielding the stated odd-order zero and counting corollary.
nonparaphrase_operation: Partial summation isolates the base oscillatory estimate; contour displacement changes zero data into arithmetic frequencies; stationary-phase localization and an explicit error budget control cancellation; the same integral under a constant-sign hypothesis becomes noncancelling and conflicts with a second contour main term.
limits: Section 4 reuses the integral-analysis pattern from Section 3 rather than invoking Theorem 3.1 as a black-box implication. Section 3 is stated under RH for a simpler formulation but says the argument is not essentially dependent on it; the Section 4 conclusion is many critical-line zeros, not RH. Exact powers, interval lengths, endpoint conventions, and constants are OCR-fragile, so only the qualitative dependency and proof architecture are retained.
quality_reason: Accepted because the four units support a specific cross-section transfer of method and proof burden: u14-u15 construct the localization machinery, while u16-u17 use its oscillatory-integral structure inside a distinct sign-change contradiction.
